title: Chelsea performance against Brighton was ‘indefensible’, says Liam Rosenior – ‘Something needs to change’
content:
Chelsea manager Liam Rosenior called his team’s 3-0 defeat to Brighton “the most difficult night” of his career, and said his players’ performance was “indefensible” and “unacceptable”.

After their loss to Brighton, Chelsea sit seventh in the Premier League table, and the chances of a top-five finish to secure Champions League football look extremely slim. Four teams behind them are within two points of them with a game in hand, raising concerns they could miss out on European qualification altogether.

Ferdi Kadioglu opened the scoring after just three minutes, before Jack Hinshelwood added a second early in the second half and Danny Welbeck added to Chelsea’s misery in stoppage time. Chelsea registered six shots, none of them on target.

“That was unacceptable,” Rosenior said, speaking to Sky Sports after the match. “In every aspect of the game, unacceptable, in attitude. I keep coming out and defending the players. That’s indefensible, that performance tonight. The manner of the goals we conceded, the amount of duels that we lost, the lack of intensity in the team. And yeah, something needs to change drastically here right now.”

“Whether you’re playing for this club, at this elite football club, or any football club, to be even accused of throwing the towel in is unacceptable. That’s all I’m going to say. I’m hurting, I feel numb. Because that doesn’t represent me. That doesn’t represent the football club in any way. That has to change, starting with the FA Cup semi-final on Sunday.

“I have discussed in depth about how this club — regardless of who is the manager — what needs to happen at this football club for this club to be where it needs to be. It’s not about me. It’s about this football club, Chelsea represents fight, spirit and determination and that was lacking in every department this evening.

“For me, I will pick a team on Sunday that represent the club in the correct manner.”

Asked in his post-match press conference about negative chants directed at him form the Chelsea supporters, Rosenior said: “I understand why the fans are frustrated. I’m frustrated with the performances we’re putting in.”

“It’s not about playing for me. It’s about playing for the club. It’s about playing for the shirt,” Rosenior said, asked whether he felt the players were ‘not playing for him’. “It’s about playing to win games of football. I can speak on what I saw tonight. You can read anything into it that you want, whether they’re playing for me or not, but that performance in itself was damning. It stood everything against what I believe in.”

“We’ll find out (whether the players can take that criticism). I haven’t criticised them up till now. I’ve defended them. They’ve deserved that. But I will tell the truth. I always come out here and tell the truth. And I blame myself as well. It’s not just blaming the players. I’m part of that process.”

Rosenior has overseen 11 wins, two draws and 10 losses in all competitions since taking charge of Chelsea in January.

Chelsea face Leeds United at Wembley on Sunday for a place in the FA Cup final.
